key_insight: Syndrome records alone can be used in post-processing to cancel logical errors in quantum circuits without learning the noise model or modifying the executed circuit.
engineering_relevance: This enables bias-free logical error mitigation for early fault-tolerant quantum algorithms with lower experimental complexity and reduced reliance on prior calibration.
method: Use only measured syndrome records as the input for classical post-processing.
Pair a fast experimental decoder with a more accurate high-complexity decoder offline.
Apply virtual error cancellation to estimate unbiased logical observables after execution.
evidence_signal: In simulations of a distance-7 rotated surface code, the dual-decoder protocol showed error decreasing with sample count and achieved more than three orders of magnitude suppression versus the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable regime.
watch_item: The approach still depends on decoder quality and may incur substantial classical post-processing and sampling overhead in practical deployments.
paper_title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
